lessons.title: Identifying High-Yielding Yam Varieties
lessons.body:
High-yielding yam varieties can produce 20 to 30 tonnes per hectare, compared to local varieties that often yield only 8 to 12 tonnes. In West Africa, the most common species are White Yam (Dioscorea rotundata), Yellow Yam (D. cayenensis), Water Yam (D. alata), and Trifoliate Yam (D. dumetorum). White yam is preferred for pounded yam and has varieties like 'TDr 89/02665' (often called 'TDr 89') that mature in 8-9 months and yield up to 25 tonnes/ha. Yellow yam, such as 'Puna' and 'Lokoja', matures in 10-12 months and stores well. Water yam varieties like 'TDa 291' and 'TDa 98/01176' are high-yielding but need more moisture. Trifoliate yam is drought-tolerant and matures in 7-8 months.

To identify a high-yielding variety, look at the leaves, stems, and tubers. White yam has dark green, heart-shaped leaves and a spiny stem; its tubers are cylindrical with white flesh. Yellow yam has yellow flesh and a more branched tuber. Water yam has broad, winged stems and tubers with brown skin and white or purple flesh. Ask local extension officers or visit a research station like IITA in Ibadan, Nigeria, or CSIR-CRI in Ghana to see demonstration plots. Yield is also influenced by soil fertility, spacing, and staking. Plant on ridges or mounds at 1 m by 1 m spacing for large tubers. Use 2.5 to 3 tonnes of seed yams per hectare.

Record your harvest: weigh tubers from a 10-plant sample and multiply by the total plant population. If you plant 10,000 plants and each yields 2.5 kg, you get 25 tonnes/ha. Compare varieties over two seasons before deciding. Avoid mixing varieties in one plot because they have different maturity times. High-yielding varieties are not always the best for your marketâsome consumers prefer specific tastes or textures. Test small plots first.

lessons.title: Selecting Healthy Seed Yams (Setts) for Planting
lessons.body:
Healthy seed yams, also called setts, are the foundation of a good harvest. A good sett weighs 200 to 500 grams, is firm, and has at least two viable buds (eyes). Never plant a sett that is soft, wrinkled, or has holes from yam beetles. Cut setts from the head (proximal end) of the tuber because it has more buds and sprouts faster. Use a sharp, clean knife or machete; dip it in 10% bleach solution between cuts to prevent disease spread. Each sett should be 5 to 10 cm long and 3 to 5 cm thick. For ware yam production, use whole small tubers (200-300 g) or cut larger tubers into setts. For seed yam production, use smaller setts (80-150 g) to multiply seed.

After cutting, treat setts to prevent rot. Dip them in a fungicide solution such as Benlate (benomyl) at 2 g per litre of water for 5 minutes, or use wood ash or a slurry of cow dung. Then allow them to dry in a shaded, well-ventilated area for 24 to 48 hours. This healing process (curing) forms a protective layer. Plant within 3 days. If you must store, keep setts in a cool, dry place with good airflowânever in sealed plastic bags. Inspect regularly and remove any rotting setts.

Select setts from healthy mother plants that showed no signs of mosaic virus, anthracnose, or nematode damage. Avoid setts from tubers that were stored for more than 4 months, as they lose vigour. For best results, buy certified seed yams from approved sources. If you save your own seed, select tubers from your best-performing plants, not from the market. A good practice is to plant a seed yam multiplication plot each year, using small setts to produce clean seed for the next season.

lessons.title: Seed Yam Treatment and Storage
lessons.body:
Proper treatment and storage of seed yams reduce losses from rot, insects, and sprouting. After harvest, cure seed yams in a shaded, well-ventilated shed for 7 to 14 days. Spread them in a single layer on wooden pallets or dry grassânever on bare ground. Curing heals wounds and thickens the skin. Then treat with a fungicide-insecticide mixture: for example, mix 50 g of benomyl (Benlate) and 50 g of actellic (pirimiphos-methyl) in 10 litres of water. Dip tubers for 2 minutes, then dry in shade. This controls storage rot and yam beetles. Alternatively, use neem leaf extract: pound 1 kg of fresh neem leaves, soak in 5 litres of water for 24 hours, strain, and dip tubers for 5 minutes.

Store seed yams in a yam barn, which is a wooden or bamboo structure with shelves, raised off the ground and thatched for shade. Keep temperature between 15Â°C and 20Â°C and relative humidity at 60-70%. In the barn, place tubers in single layers on shelves, not piled. Inspect every two weeks and remove any sprouting, rotting, or insect-damaged tubers. Sprouting can be reduced by storing in darkness and cool conditions. If you have only a few tubers, store them in a ventilated basket in a dark room. Never store seed yams in the same room as onions or potatoesâthey release gases that promote sprouting.

For long-term storage (4-6 months), you can use a pit storage method: dig a pit 1 m deep, line with dry grass, place tubers in layers, cover with more grass and soil, leaving a small ventilation hole. Check monthly. Another option is cold storage at 12-15Â°C if available. Always keep records: date of storage, number of tubers, and any treatments. Before planting, re-inspect and discard any soft or mouldy setts. Healthy seed yams should be firm, with no odour, and buds intact.

lessons.title: Certified Seed Sources and Quality Assurance
lessons.body:
Certified seed yams are produced under strict quality control by national research institutions and registered seed growers. In Nigeria, the National Agricultural Seeds Council (NASC) certifies seed yams through the Seed Certification and Quality Control Service. In Ghana, the Plant Protection and Regulatory Services Directorate (PPRSD) does the same. Certified seed comes with a blue or green label showing the variety name, lot number, germination percentage (for yams, this is sprouting percentage), and date of testing. Always buy from authorised dealers, research institutes (IITA, CSIR-CRI, NCRI), or accredited seed companies. Avoid buying from open markets unless you know the source.

Quality assurance checks include: (1) physical purityâno stones, soil, or other varieties; (2) healthâfree from visible disease symptoms like mosaic, anthracnose, or nematode galls; (3) vigourâfirm tubers with intact buds; and (4) trueness to typeâtubers match the variety description. For yams, a certified seed lot must have less than 2% disease incidence and less than 5% off-types. Ask for a certificate of analysis from the seller. If buying in bulk, take a random sample of 10 tubers and cut them open to check for internal rot or brown discolouration.

Certified seed yams cost moreâoften 2 to 3 times the price of farmer-saved seedâbut they give higher yields and reduce disease risk. For example, a 100 kg bag of certified TDr 89 setts may cost 30,000 to 45,000 Naira (about $40-60), while farmer-saved seed might cost 10,000 to 15,000 Naira. However, certified seed can increase yield by 30-50%, making it profitable. To ensure quality, buy from a seller who can show you the seed production plot. Join a seed growers' cooperative to access certified seed at lower prices. Always keep your receipt and the label for traceability.

lessons.title: Adapting Varieties to Local Conditions
lessons.body:
No single yam variety is best everywhere. You must match the variety to your local climate, soil, and market. Rainfall is key: white yam (D. rotundata) needs 1000-1500 mm of rain and a 7-9 month growing season. Water yam (D. alata) needs more than 1500 mm and can tolerate waterlogging, making it suitable for swampy areas. Yellow yam (D. cayenensis) is more drought-tolerant and does well in forest-savanna transition zones. Trifoliate yam (D. dumetorum) is the most drought-tolerant and can grow in drier savannas with 800-1000 mm rainfall. If you are in a dry area, choose early-maturing varieties like 'TDr 89' (8 months) or trifoliate yam (7 months).

Soil type matters: yams prefer deep, well-drained loamy soils with pH 5.5-6.5. Heavy clay soils cause tuber deformation. If your soil is sandy, add organic matter like poultry manure (5-10 tonnes/ha) to improve water holding. For acidic soils (pH below 5.5), apply lime at 1-2 tonnes/ha before planting. In areas with nematode problems, plant resistant varieties such as 'TDr 95/19177' or rotate with cereals. Also consider market preference: in some regions, consumers want white yam for pounded yam; in others, water yam is preferred for boiling. Visit your local market and ask traders which varieties sell best.

Test new varieties on a small plot (0.1 ha) for one season before expanding. Compare yield, disease resistance, and storage life. Keep records of rainfall, soil type, and inputs. If a variety fails, try another. Participate in farmer field schools or extension demonstrations to see how different varieties perform. Adapting varieties is not just about yieldâit's about reducing risk and meeting local demand. For example, in the derived savanna of Nigeria, farmers often plant a mix of white yam and yellow yam to spread harvest and market risks.

lessons.title: Cost and Availability of Different Seed Yams
lessons.body:
Seed yam costs vary by variety, size, and source. In West Africa, a 100 kg bag of farmer-saved white yam setts (200-300 g each) costs between 10,000 and 20,000 Naira ($13-27) in Nigeria, or 150-300 Ghana Cedis ($13-26) in Ghana. Certified seed yams of improved varieties like TDr 89 or TDa 291 cost 30,000 to 50,000 Naira ($40-67) per 100 kg. Yellow yam seed is often cheaper, 8,000-15,000 Naira per 100 kg, because it is less popular. Water yam seed is intermediate, 15,000-25,000 Naira. Trifoliate yam seed is scarce and can cost 20,000-30,000 Naira per 100 kg. Prices are higher during planting season (February-April) and lower after harvest (November-January).

Availability depends on your location. In Nigeria, major seed yam producing areas include Benue, Taraba, and Nasarawa states. In Ghana, the northern regions (Northern, Upper East, Upper West) produce most seed yams. If you are far from these areas, transport costs add 10-20%. You can also produce your own seed yams by planting small setts (80-150 g) in a dedicated plot. This reduces cost and ensures quality. A 0.1 ha seed yam plot can produce 1,000-1,500 seed yams (about 200-300 kg) in one season, enough to plant 0.5-0.7 ha of ware yam. Start with certified seed once, then multiply.

To reduce costs, join a cooperative or farmer group to buy in bulk. Some research institutes sell seed yams at subsidised prices to farmers. For example, IITA sells breeder seed to registered seed growers, who then multiply and sell to farmers. Always compare prices from at least three sources. Remember that cheap seed from unknown sources often carries disease and gives poor yields. Invest in quality seedâit is the cheapest input in the long run. Keep a record of your seed costs per hectare to calculate profit.

lessons.title: Practical Reference
lessons.body:
Practical Reference: Yam Varieties and Seed Selection

Yam (Dioscorea spp.) is one of West Africa's most valuable food and cash crops, with Nigeria alone producing roughly two-thirds of global output. For the commercial grower, however, the difference between profit and loss is decided long before planting: it is decided by which variety you choose and the quality of the seed yams (setts) you put in the ground. Seed material typically represents 30â50% of total yam production costs, making variety and seed selection the single highest-leverage decision in the yam value chain.

This Practical Reference consolidates the six lessons of this module into a working field and business guide. Use it alongside the individual lessons as a decision-support tool.

1. Varieties: Matching Market to Field

Yam varieties fall into market-driven categories. Dioscorea rotundata (white yam) dominates West African commercial trade, with popular improved and landrace varieties including TDr 89/02665, TDr 95/19177, TDr 95/18544, and the widely grown landraces like Efuru, Nwaopoko, and Amula. D. alata (water yam) offers higher yields and better storage under some conditions, while D. cayenensis (yellow yam) commands premium prices in certain urban markets due to its colour and taste.

For business planning, the key is not "which variety is best" in the abstract, but which variety delivers the highest net margin per hectare for your target market. Pounded yam processors pay a premium for high-dry-matter white yam; fryers and chip processors favour varieties with low sugar and high starch; exporters need uniform tuber shape and consistent sizing.

2. Seed Yam Selection: The Quality Filters

Healthy seed yams (setts) determine germination, vigour, and final yield. The following filters should be applied at purchase and again at planting:

  • Size: 200â400 g setts are optimal for commercial production; smaller setts reduce yield, larger setts waste money.
  • Shape: Uniform, cylindrical setts with at least two viable buds (eyes).
  • Skin: Free from cracks, rot, nematode galls, and mealybug colonies.
  • Flesh: Creamy-white to pale yellow, firm, no brown discolouration (indicating infection).
  • Age: 3â5 months post-harvest; very old setts have low viability, very fresh setts may not have broken dormancy.

3. Seed Treatment and Storage

Treatment reduces losses from fungal rot, nematodes, and insects. Common practices include dipping setts in a fungicide-insecticide slurry (e.g., benomyl + chlorpyrifos) or, for organic growers, coating with wood ash and neem extract. After treatment, setts should be cured in a shaded, ventilated area for 7â14 days to allow wound healing before storage or planting.

Storage must be in a well-ventilated, raised barn or crib, protected from rodents and direct sunlight. Properly stored seed yams can maintain viability for 3â5 months with losses under 10%. Poor storage can cause 30â50% losses â a direct hit to your input budget.

â  SAFETY WARNING: Pesticide Handling

Fungicides and insecticides used in sett treatment are toxic. Always wear gloves, boots, and a face mask. Never eat, drink, or smoke during treatment. Store chemicals in locked cabinets away from food and children. Dispose of empty containers through approved channels â never reuse them for water or food. Follow national pesticide regulations (e.g., NAFDAC in Nigeria, EPA in Ghana).

4. Certified Seed Sources and Quality Assurance

Africa's certified seed yam sector is expanding rapidly through the YIIFSWA project and national seed councils. Certified seed carries a label confirming variety purity, phytosanitary status, and germination viability. Buying certified seed costs 15â30% more than farm-saved seed but typically delivers 20â40% higher yields and reduces disease carry-over. For commercial growers, this is a sound investment.

Key sources include:

  • IITA and partner seed companies (Nigeria, Ghana, Benin)
  • National Agricultural Seed Councils (NASC Nigeria, CSIR-Ghana)
  • Community-based seed producers registered with national programmes
  • AfricaYam project partners

5. Adapting Varieties to Local Conditions

Variety performance is location-specific. A variety that yields 30 t/ha in Ibadan may yield 18 t/ha in a drier or nematode-infested field. Before committing to a variety, run a small on-farm trial (0.1â0.2 ha) across at least one full season. Record yield, disease incidence, and market acceptance. This "ground-truthing" step protects your investment.

6. Cost and Availability of Different Seed Yams

Seed yam prices vary by variety, sett size, season, and region. The table below provides indicative 2023â2024 West African market data for planning purposes.

Table 1: Indicative Seed Yam Prices and Yield Potential (West Africa, 2023â2024)
Variety / Type Species Avg. Yield (t/ha) Seed Cost (USD/kg) Market Preference
TDr 89/02665 D. rotundata 25â35 1.20â1.80 High (pounded yam)
TDr 95/19177 D. rotundata 28â38 1.30â1.90 High (dual purpose)
Efuru (landrace) D. rotundata 18â25 0.80â1.20 Very high (local)
Water yam (TDa) D. alata 30â45 1.00â1.50 Medium (processing)
Yellow yam D. cayenensis 20â30 1.50â2.20 Premium (urban)

Source: IITA YIIFSWA Market and Seed System Studies (2023); FAO FAOSTAT Yam Production Data (2022); NASC Nigeria Seed Price Survey (2023). Prices are indicative and vary by region and season.

Table 2: Seed Yam Quality Indicators and Acceptable Thresholds
Indicator Acceptable Range Reject If Business Impact
Sett weight 200â400 g <150 g or >500 g Lower yield or wasted input
Viable buds â¥ 2 per sett < 2 buds Poor germination
Skin condition Smooth, no lesions Cracks, galls, rot Disease carry-over
Flesh colour Cream to pale yellow Brown or black spots Rot during storage
Storage loss < 10% over 3 months > 15% Direct financial loss

Source: IITA Seed Yam Quality Standards (2018); AfricaYam Project Technical Bulletin (2020); FAO Yam Seed Systems Guidelines (2019).

Quick Reference Checklist

  1. Define your market first â pounded yam, chips, export, or local fresh market â then choose the variety that serves it.
  2. Buy certified seed from NASC/CSIR-registered producers; verify the label for variety, batch, and phytosanitary status.
  3. Inspect every sett before purchase: 200â400 g, â¥2 buds, no cracks, no rot, firm flesh.
  4. Treat setts with approved fungicide/insecticide or wood ash + neem; wear full protective gear.
  5. Cure for 7â14 days in a shaded, ventilated area before storage or planting.
  6. Store in raised, ventilated barns; target <10% loss over 3 months; inspect monthly.
  7. Run a small on-farm trial of any new variety before scaling up to commercial acreage.
  8. Calculate break-even yield before planting: (total input cost) Ã· (farm-gate price per tonne). If expected yield is below this, change variety or seed source.

Further Reading

  • IITA â Yam Improvement for Income and Food Security in West Africa (YIIFSWA) â technical guides, variety descriptions, and seed system resources.
  • FAO FAOSTAT â Yam Production and Trade Data â country-level production, yield, and price statistics.
  • National Agricultural Seed Council (NASC), Nigeria â certified seed producer lists and quality standards.
  • CGIAR â AfricaYam Project â breeding, agronomy, and seed system research outputs.
  • AfricaYam â Variety and Seed Information Portal â variety performance data across West African agro-ecologies.

This module is part of the RISE AFRICA Skills programme. Content is aligned with IITA, FAO, and national seed council guidelines. Always verify current prices and regulations with local extension services before making commercial decisions.

quiz.q: Which yam variety is known for high yield and matures in 8-9 months?
quiz.explanation: TDr 89 is a white yam variety that matures in 8-9 months and can yield up to 25 tonnes per hectare.

quiz.q: What is the recommended weight of a good seed yam sett?
quiz.explanation: A good sett weighs 200 to 500 grams, is firm, and has at least two viable buds.

quiz.q: Which part of the yam tuber is best for cutting setts because it has more buds?
quiz.explanation: The head (proximal end) of the tuber has more buds and sprouts faster.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of curing seed yams before storage?
options: B) To heal wounds and thicken skin
quiz.explanation: Curing heals wounds and thickens the skin, reducing rot during storage.

quiz.q: Which chemical is commonly used to treat seed yams against rot?
quiz.explanation: Benlate (benomyl) is a fungicide used to dip setts and prevent rot.

quiz.q: What is the ideal temperature range for storing seed yams?
quiz.explanation: Seed yams store best at 15-20Â°C with 60-70% relative humidity.

quiz.q: Which organisation certifies seed yams in Nigeria?
quiz.explanation: The National Agricultural Seeds Council (NASC) certifies seed yams in Nigeria.

quiz.q: What percentage of disease incidence is allowed in a certified seed yam lot?
quiz.explanation: Certified seed yam lots must have less than 2% disease incidence.

quiz.q: Which yam species is most drought-tolerant?
quiz.explanation: Trifoliate yam (D. dumetorum) is the most drought-tolerant and can grow in drier savannas.

quiz.q: What is the ideal soil pH for yam production?
quiz.explanation: Yams prefer deep, well-drained loamy soils with pH 5.5-6.5.

quiz.q: How much does a 100 kg bag of certified white yam seed cost in Nigeria?
quiz.explanation: Certified seed yams of improved varieties cost 30,000 to 50,000 Naira per 100 kg.

quiz.q: Which state in Nigeria is a major seed yam producing area?
quiz.explanation: Benue, Taraba, and Nasarawa states are major seed yam producing areas in Nigeria.

quiz.q: What is the recommended spacing for planting yam to get large tubers?
quiz.explanation: Planting on ridges or mounds at 1 m by 1 m spacing allows large tuber development.

quiz.q: Which of these is a sign of a healthy seed yam sett?
quiz.explanation: Healthy setts are firm, have no odour, and buds are intact.

quiz.q: What is the first step after cutting yam setts?
options: D) Dry in sun for 1 week
quiz.explanation: After cutting, setts should be dipped in a fungicide solution to prevent rot.

quiz.q: How long should setts be dried in shade after treatment?
quiz.explanation: Setts should be dried in a shaded, well-ventilated area for 24 to 48 hours.

quiz.q: Which yam variety is preferred for pounded yam in many parts of West Africa?
quiz.explanation: White yam is preferred for pounded yam due to its texture and taste.

quiz.q: What is a yam barn?
options: A) A storage structure with shelves
quiz.explanation: A yam barn is a wooden or bamboo structure with shelves for storing yams.

quiz.q: How often should you inspect stored seed yams?
quiz.explanation: Inspect stored seed yams every two weeks and remove any rotting or sprouting tubers.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a quality assurance check for certified seed yams?
quiz.explanation: Quality checks include physical purity, health, vigour, and trueness to type, not label colour.

quiz.q: What is the advantage of certified seed yams over farmer-saved seed?
options: B) Higher yield and less disease
quiz.explanation: Certified seed gives higher yields and reduces disease risk, though it costs more.

quiz.q: Which yam species needs more than 1500 mm of rainfall?
quiz.explanation: Water yam (D. alata) needs more than 1500 mm of rain and can tolerate waterlogging.

quiz.q: What is a recommended practice to reduce nematode problems in yam?
quiz.explanation: Rotating with cereals helps reduce nematode populations in the soil.

quiz.q: How much seed yam is needed to plant 1 hectare of yam?
quiz.explanation: Use 2.5 to 3 tonnes of seed yams per hectare for planting.

quiz.q: Which of these is a sign of a high-yielding yam variety?
options: B) Cylindrical tubers with white flesh
quiz.explanation: High-yielding white yam varieties typically have cylindrical tubers with white flesh.

quiz.q: What is the best time to buy seed yams to get lower prices?
quiz.explanation: Prices are lower after harvest, from November to January.

quiz.q: Which of these is a method for long-term storage of seed yams?
quiz.explanation: Pit storage is a traditional method for long-term storage of seed yams.

quiz.q: What is the recommended treatment for setts using neem leaf extract?
quiz.explanation: Dip setts in neem leaf extract for 5 minutes to control pests and diseases.

quiz.q: Which organisation in Ghana certifies seed yams?
quiz.explanation: The Plant Protection and Regulatory Services Directorate (PPRSD) certifies seed yams in Ghana.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of producing your own seed yams?
options: A) Reduces cost and ensures quality
quiz.explanation: Producing your own seed yams reduces cost and ensures you have quality seed.
